newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium to start withdrawing troops from Congo.
newsitem.headline: Belgium to start withdrawing troops from Congo.

text.p: Belgium will start repatriating some of its paratroops from Brazaville in the coming days, Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Thursday.

"The government has decided to progressively withdraw our troops from Congo-Brazzaville. A first contingent of 200 to 250 men will return within 24 to 48 hours," Dehaene told a news conference after a cabinet meeting.
In March, Belgium sent 693 paratroops to Brazzaville, the capital of Congo, which lies just across the Zaire river from Kinshasa, the capital of the new Democratic Republic of Congo (formerly Zaire).
They were on stand-by to evacuate the 1,500 Belgians living in Kinshasa if they came under attack during the revolution led by Laurent Kabila that ousted President Mobutu Sese Seko at the weekend.

Dehaene said that the rest of the Belgian troops would be withdrawn in the coming weeks, depending on the situation in Bas-Zaire, a region in the west of the Democratic Republic of Congo, which is not yet completely under the control of the new regime and which has some Belgian residents.
